scope: Focused second consideration of estimator distinctions, UDP loss presentation, route/provenance links, and preservation limitations after round-one row-by-row comparison.

challenged.question: Could UDP median loss be presented as aggregate loss?
challenged.evidence: report.html explicitly labels loss as median of seven per-round loss rates. Independently summing the seven official SS2022/freedom upload round counters in summary-udp.json gives 12,390 lost of 97,664 offered datagrams = 12.686353211009175% aggregate; the median of the seven listed rates is 12.413990825688073%. The report labels these as different statistics. The 3,906,560 / 3,807,198 / 99,362 cohort aggregate counters are separately labeled non-median totals.
challenged.disposition: Estimator distinction is accurate; no change warranted.

challenged.question: Could pooled RTT/setup or connection/setup response substitute for established RTT?
challenged.evidence: The report identifies established RTT as median of seven round medians over 256 verified 64-byte samples per round, lists fresh first response separately from eight fresh-flow samples per round, and says pooled 1,792 RTT / 56 setup samples do not replace primary estimators. Separate TCP/UDP tables expose upload, download, RTT and first-response columns.

challenged.question: Could UDP appear to represent unpaced capacity or silently omit its drain/control overhead?
challenged.evidence: The report labels UDP as a separate loss-aware application workload, names reliable same-route control and exact 100 ms receiver drain/cutoff, includes drain/control/barrier overhead in goodput, and explicitly disclaims raw capacity and comparison against TCP capacity.

challenged.question: Does the report overstate preservation or isolate batching causally?
challenged.evidence: The report calls the comparison whole-product with source/dependency/lifecycle/SS2022 confounds, discloses fixed support CPU contention, distinguishes TCP fwupd.service disappearance (cause unknown) from unchanged UDP service snapshots, and states contemporaneous manual/container Xray PID/command identity was not captured.
challenged.disposition: No causal or host-preservation overclaim found.

independent_html_and_link_check.self_contained_static_rendering: One inline style block; zero script, image, or SVG tags.

remaining_limits: The report remains a same-host isolated whole-product benchmark, not WAN performance or causal attribution to batching/GSO.
CPU sharing can bottleneck fixed support processes.
Cause of the observed fwupd disappearance and contemporaneous manual/container Xray PID identity remain unobserved, explicitly disclosed limitations.
changes_from_round_one: No report, summary, or measurement values changed. This round challenged primary-vs-aggregate UDP loss and established-vs-pooled/setup latency interpretation; review evidence was extended without replacing round-one evidence.
result: Accepted. No numeric, statistical-label, route-link, or reviewed limitation-disclosure discrepancy found.
